macros.name: carryline
macros.doc: \carryline takes two arguments, the number of digits you’ll be putting carries over, and the line with the carries or borrows that you wish to display.

macros.name: fractionsymbol
macros.doc: With basicarith, you can use any symbol you want; the default is “;”, but by redefining \fractionsymbol, you can get anything else.

macros.name: longdiv
macros.doc: The \longdiv macro is, obviously, the most important; it typesets the allimportant first line of a long division problem.

macros.name: nextldline
macros.doc: In the American style of long division, intermediate values are placed underneath the dividend, while the solution itself is placed above it. \nextldline typesets these intermediate values.

macros.name: noopline
macros.doc: \noopline is identical to \opline except that it does not print the operator.

macros.name: strike
macros.doc: basicarith provides the \strike command, which will strike out a borrow when another borrow is required.
